newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark's DFDS says 96 profits soar.
newsitem.headline: Denmark's DFDS says 96 profits soar.

text.p: Danish shipping group J.Lauritzen's DFDS ferry and freight unit on Tuesday reported 1996 pre-tax profits of 271.1 million crowns compared to 106.1 million the year before.

A DFDS statement said that overall passenger traffic on its Scandinavian Seaways ferry division rose, despite the removal of one ship, the chartering out of another during the high season and the closure of two routes.

All-round sea, road and air freight division DFDS Transport logged a slight rise in earnings, it said, despite a fall in German traffic and weak sterling against the Danish crown in the the first half of 1996. Sterling firmed in the second half.
Its Tor Line North Sea cargo business carried 13 percent more freight than in 1995, helped by the construction of a new terminal at the British port of Immingham, it added.

DFDS said that 1997 was likely to be marked by tough competition but it expected to replicate the strong 1996 result. It recommended a rise in dividend for the unit share to nine percent, from 1995's six percent.
J. Lauritzen group results are due on a so-far unspecified date later this month. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969650
